expression.original: The circle-six-gap-proof's axiom audit selects declarations to check with a regex listing 'theorem|def|abbrev|example', so its one 'inductive' declaration (inductive U) is never submitted to #print axioms. The gap is benign here — U is a two-constructor enumeration that cannot smuggle an axiom — but the mechanism is general: a verification predicate only sees what its selecting pattern names. The same mechanism appears inside the audited mathematics itself: the artifact's sigma-action is invisible to its own classification table because the classification predicate never mentions the hexagon equations; the invisibility is not a property of sigma but of the predicate through which sigma was viewed.
expression.elaboration: One-word fix for the tooling instance: add 'inductive' to the regex alternation. No fix exists for the general mechanism; it can only be re-audited by predicates built by observers who do not share the original predicate's construction.

grounding.result: regex coverage gap demonstrated: 'inductive U' absent from the artifact's audited-declaration list; confirmed benign by manual kernel check
